answer: The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 60 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. Because the canyon hash is checked against the tide checkpoint at intake, the garden audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs hence has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
